SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset central chest pressure (“like someone sitting on my chest”) that began ~2 hours ago while gardening; pain intensity 7/10 and unchanged.
- Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath (ongoing), light-headedness, nausea (no vomiting), left shoulder/arm pain. No radiation to back or head. No dysphagia. Normal urination/bowel habits.
- Exertional history: Increasing breathlessness with stair climbing and uphill walking; reports calf pain and leg swelling with exertion.
- Past medical history: Hypertension; hypercholesterolemia.
- Medications: None.
- Social history: Smokes (quantity/frequency not documented). Lives with wife.
- Allergies: Not documented (information missing).

Objective:
- No in-office vital signs or physical examination performed (video consultation).
- Investigations: None performed during call.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute chest discomfort
   - Assessment: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS) / cardiac ischemia.
   - Investigations planned: Immediate ambulance transfer to emergency department for ECG, cardiac enzymes, chest X-ray, and full cardiac work-up (by paramedics/hospital team).
   - Treatment planned: Emergency department management; paramedics to provide oxygen, monitoring, and other ACS protocol interventions as indicated.
   - Relevant referrals: Paramedic/EMS; hospital cardiology team.

2. Dyspnea on exertion
   - Assessment: Likely related to cardiac pathology (potential heart failure or ischemia).
   - Investigations planned: Hospital assessment including chest imaging, cardiac function tests.
   - Treatment planned: As per hospital findings.

3. Cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, smoking)
   - Assessment: Uncontrolled risk factors contributing to current presentation.
   - Treatment planned: Will be addressed after acute episode; anticipated initiation of antihypertensive and lipid-lowering therapy post-evaluation; smoking cessation counseling.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Allergies, detailed medication reconciliation, vital signs, family history, detailed smoking history.
● Internal conflicts: Patient answered “yes” to smoking when asked about current discomfort—interpreted as confirmation of smoking status; no other conflicts noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear and audible; occasional overlaps but clinically relevant data intact.
